title: Conditional raw localization embedding of a bounded Hom-continuous subcategory
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $A$ a commutative ring, $t\in A$, and $R$ a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories with integer shifts and cohomology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Put $R_t=R[1/t]$, the sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], and let $F:D(R)\to D(R_t)$ be exact scalar localization $R_t\otimes_R^L-$, with sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and its termwise induced triangulated shift comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Let $\mathcal C\subset D(R)$ be a full $A$-linear subcategory [def-weil-linear-category] stable under all integer shifts, whose objects are bounded below. Suppose each $K\in\mathcal C$ has the property that for every small countable family $(M_i)$ in $D(R)$ with a common cohomological lower bound and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the shifted-coprojection map $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(K,M_i[q])\to\operatorname{Hom}(K,(\bigoplus_iM_i)[q])$ is an isomorphism. Let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/t]$ be raw scalar localization, with unchanged objects and localized Hom modules, without idempotent completion [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For $K,L\in\mathcal C$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, the actual scalar-extension map
$$\Phi^q_{K,L}:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L[q])[1/t]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_t)}(FK,FL[q]),\qquad f/t^n\longmapsto t^{-n}F(f)$$
is an isomorphism of $A[1/t]$-modules, where the target uses the stated shift comparison. These maps are natural in both variables and commute with simultaneous integer shifts. In degree zero they define a fully faithful $A[1/t]$-linear functor [def-weil-linear-functor] $J:\mathcal C[1/t]\to D(R_t)$ with $J(QK)=FK$ and $J(f/t^n)=t^{-n}F(f)$. Explicitly, precomposition by an integral arrow $a$ sends $\Phi(f/t^n)$ to $t^{-n}F(f)F(a)$, postcomposition by $b$ sends it to $F(b)t^{-n}F(f)$, and simultaneous shift by $r$ sends it to $t^{-n}F(f)[r]$ under the canonical identifications. Identities and composable fractions satisfy $J(1/1)=1$ and
$$J((g/t^m)\circ(f/t^n))=t^{-(m+n)}F(gf)=(t^{-m}F(g))(t^{-n}F(f)).$$
These formulas apply to every localized morphism; no essential-surjectivity assertion is included.

proof.text: Fix $K,L\in\mathcal C$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-derived-hom] on the given small site with the same $A,t,R,R_t,F$. Its countable common-lower-bound Hom hypothesis is exactly the assumption on $K$, and its bounded-below target hypothesis holds for $L$. Its termwise exact scalar-localization functor is the stipulated $F$, including its shift comparisons. It therefore gives the required $A[1/t]$-linear isomorphism $\Phi^q_{K,L}$ with $f/t^n\mapsto t^{-n}F(f)$, natural in both variables and compatible with shifts.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), full-faithfulness sentence, pp. 61-62; explicit abstract conditional assembly

proof.text: Write $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(K,L)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)$, using fullness. Identify the raw Hom $H\otimes_AA[1/t]$ of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] with $H[1/t]$: the maps are $h\otimes(a/t^n)\mapsto ah/t^n$ and $h/t^n\mapsto h\otimes t^{-n}$. The first respects tensor balancing by [def-weil-module-base-change]. For the second, the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives $t^k(t^mh-t^nh\prime)=0$; multiplying its tensor by $t^{-(k+n+m)}$ gives $h\otimes t^{-n}=h\prime\otimes t^{-m}$. The two maps are inverse on generators and fractions. Thus every raw morphism is a fraction (a finite sum uses one common power denominator).

The naturality and shift clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-derived-hom] apply to the maps in Step 1. More explicitly, for integral arrows $a:K\prime\to K$ and $b:L\to L\prime$, $\Phi^q((fa)/t^n)=t^{-n}F(f)F(a)$ and $\Phi^q((b[q]f)/t^n)=F(b)[q]t^{-n}F(f)$. Under the stipulated shift identifications $\Phi^q_{K[r],L[r]}(f[r]/t^n)=t^{-n}F(f)[r]$. Here the shifted objects remain in $\mathcal C$ by shift stability. The displayed formulas are obtained by functoriality and linearity from the fraction formula, so also give the asserted equations in every degree.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), full-faithfulness sentence, pp. 61-62; explicit abstract conditional assembly

proof.text: Set $J(QK)=FK$ and let its Hom map be $\Phi^0_{K,L}$ through Step 2. It is well-defined and $A[1/t]$-linear by Step 1. The composition and identity formulas of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], together with functoriality of $F$, give $J(1/1)=F(1)=1$ and $J((g/t^m)\circ(f/t^n))=t^{-(m+n)}F(gf)=(t^{-m}F(g))(t^{-n}F(f))$. Every morphism has such a fraction representative by Step 2. These equations define a functor, linear in the sense of [def-weil-linear-functor]. Every Hom map is bijective by Step 1 at $q=0$, hence $J$ is fully faithful. Its codomain is the ambient $D(R_t)$.
